title: Parliamentary Privileges Amendment (Royal Commission Response) Bill 2022
short_title: Parliamentary Privileges Amendment (Royal Commission Response) Bill 2022

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would let royal commissions examining government draw conclusions from parliamentary material that would otherwise be restricted by specified parliamentary privilege protections.
It would create an exception to the Parliamentary Privileges Act and the Bill of Rights for admitting evidence used to draw those inferences.
The exception would cover the Defence and Veteran Suicide Royal Commission and other commissions whose terms require examining government, commencing after royal assent.
changes: The specified restriction on drawing inferences from parliamentary proceedings would no longer bar evidence in qualifying commissions.
The corresponding Bill of Rights restriction would also be displaced for that purpose.
The new exception would operate from the day following royal assent.
summary.affected: Qualifying royal commissions and the government officials they question about matters covered by parliamentary privilege would be affected.
